newsitem.title: USA: Dollar falls as rate hike hopes fade.
newsitem.headline: Dollar falls as rate hike hopes fade.

text.p: The dollar fell against most major currencies on Monday as hopes faded for a near-term increase in U.S. interest rates.

The Federal Reserve meets on Sept. 24 to decide whether to boost rates in order to keep inflation in check. However, U.S. economic data released last week indicated that price pressures at the wholesale and retail levels were in fact not getting out of hand.

"Of course, one of the reasons why the dollar had rallied ... is because of expectations the Fed would hike in September," said Brian McCarthy, market analyst at Ruesch International. "Those expectations are no longer as entrenched as they used to be."
Higher rates typically help the American currency by making dollar-denominated deposits more attractive.
In late New York trading ,the dollar slid to 1.5110 German marks from 1.5134 marks late Friday and to 110.20 Japanese yen from 110.47 yen.
The dollar's drop against the yen was largely technical as foreign exchange trading in Japan was closed for the Respect for the Aged holiday and as no market-moving U.S. economic data were released.

"Really the market is just trading technically," said David Gilmore, a partner at Foreign Exchange Analytics. "There is no real incentive in the market today and people are trying to find a bit of a base."
While fewer economists believe American interest rates are headed higher this month, some still cling to the view the Federal Reserve will probably push up rates later this year.

"If it looked like we weren't going to have a rate hike this year, then the dollar would probably back off more," said Kevin Harris, an international economist at MCM CurrencyWatch. "But currently of Fed watchers who were being surveyed, around 60 percent of them expect a rate hike in November."

A strong rally in stocks and bonds last Friday had lifted the dollar at the end of the week. Although the dollar failed to benefit from an extended stock rally Monday, the currency still got a measure of psychological support.
The Dow Jones industrial average ended 50.68 points higher at 5,889.20, its second consecutive record closing high, after soaring even higher earlier.

"It's really the stock and bond markets and their strength that's supporting the dollar at this point," McCarthy said. "If the stock and bonds stop their rally or if they undergo a little bit of profit-taking, that could be the excuse that the interbank traders are looking for to take profits on the dollar, as well as their diminished confidence in the likelihood of a rate cut this month."
The British pound climbed to $1.5578 from $1.5553, while the dollar fell to 1.2410 Swiss francs from 1.2435 francs. The U.S. currency rose slightly to Canadian $1.3705 from C$1.3699.
